newsitem.title: CHINA: China government officials made to report incomes.
newsitem.headline: China government officials made to report incomes.

text.p: Chinese authorities, wary of rising popular resentment toward official corruption, are requiring all central government officials to report their incomes, said a report available in Beijing on Sunday.
All central government offices and state organs are requiring officials to submit income reports for inspection and auditing, said the September 25 edition of the News Digest.

Officials were required to report not only their regular salaries but also any subsidies, benefits, inheritance, gifts and other sources of income, which are often worth many times more than official salaries, the newspaper said.
About 80 percent of work units at the county level or above had started to force local officials to report income, it said.

"The current income situation of cadres is more complicated than in the past and is not as unified as it was before reform and opening up," it said. "Some people worry, might cadres try to conceal their incomes?"
Reforms launched in 1979 have created loopholes in the system that have allowed many government officials to use their positions to collect vast amounts of bribes and kickbacks.
Communist Party chief Jiang Zemin has warned that corruption is a virus that threatens to undermine Beijing's rule.
